I graded Riley's submission `s2` for quiz 0001 and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`: 3 correct, 2 partial, 1 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | You know what makes a system an agent: the loop. |
| q2 | correct | The model outputs a request naming the tool; the program runs it. |
| q3 | wrong (M6) | "It will eventually fix the bug" is wrong. A repeating failure needs a stopping condition such as a step limit, which also caps your model spend. |
| q4 | partial (M4) | 4 is the right count. But "the model runs the tools" is not how it works: the program runs each tool and calls the model again with the result. |
| q5 | correct | You gave both parts, the result goes back as the next input and the model uses it to decide what to do. |
| q6 | partial | The name is only part of it. The model chooses from the whole tool description: name, purpose and parameters. |

You have the core of the loop down. Two things need work: the program, not the model, runs the tools, and a loop needs a way to stop.

I also added learning record `0003` and updated `NOTES.md`. `s1` is still ungraded.

**Next step:** write a one-sentence description for `check_calendar` (what it does and what it takes), and pick a step limit for the makerspace assistant. Then we can move on to context and memory.
